newsitem.title: USA: Honeywell and Measurex to merge.
newsitem.headline: Honeywell and Measurex to merge.

text.p: Honeywell Inc and Measurex Corp said they reached a definitive agreement to merge in an all-cash transaction valued at about $600 million.

The transaction is expected to greatly strengthen Honeywell's position as a supplier of systems, services and products for the worldwide pulp and paper manufacturing industry, the companies said in a joint statement.

Under the terms of the agreement, which was approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Honeywell this week will commence an all-cash tender offer for all outstanding shares of Measurex stock at a price of $35 per share.

"Today's announcement signals a major step that will broaden Honeywell's base in the important pulp and paper industry," said Michael Bonsignore, chairman and chief executive officer of Honeywell, in a statement.

"We see this transaction as a way to unite the particular strengths of each of our companies," said David Bossen, chairman and chief executive officer of Measurex, in a statement. "In this way, we'll be able to deliver a complete suite of automation solutions for pulp and paper manufacturers, extending from the woodyard to the shipping dock."

Honeywell provides industrial automation and control, including process control applications for the pulping industry, and a broad range of instrumentation. Measurex is a large provider of paper machine integrated control systems.
The merger should provide opportunities for stronger growth for Honeywell in the pulp and paper industry as well as reductions in costs, Bonsignore said.

The business unit will be run within Honeywell Industrial Automation and Control by John Gingerich, who has been president of Measurex. He will report to Markos Tambakeras, president of Honeywell Industrial Control.
